prompt:
A mechatronics engineer is analysing vibration in a 4-pole, 37 kW three-phase induction motor driving a centrifugal pump via a rigid coupling. The motor operates at 1475 RPM (50 Hz supply, 1.67% slip). The motor has 48 stator slots and 38 rotor bars.

The engineer identifies the electromagnetic radial force harmonics using the formula: f_force = (k1 * Z_r * (1-s)/p +/- k2) * f_supply, where Z_r = 38 (rotor bars), s = 0.0167 (slip), p = 2 (pole pairs), f_supply = 50 Hz, and k1, k2 are integers. For k1 = 1, k2 = 0, this gives f_force = 38 * (1-0.0167)/2 * 50 = 38 * 0.4958 * 50 = 942.1 Hz. The engineer identifies this as the principal slot harmonic force frequency.

The motor is mounted on a fabricated steel base frame, and the engineer has performed a modal analysis of the combined motor-base assembly. The first three natural frequencies are measured as: 145 Hz (rocking mode), 480 Hz (vertical bending), and 938 Hz (base plate drumming mode).

The engineer notes that the 942.1 Hz electromagnetic force is close to the 938 Hz structural mode and recommends stiffening the base plate to raise the drumming mode frequency. The stiffening involves welding additional ribs to increase the drumming mode to 1050 Hz. No other vibration mitigation is proposed.

seeded_faults.description: The electromagnetic force frequency formula used is incorrect. Radial electromagnetic forces in induction motors are produced by the interaction of stator and rotor MMF harmonics, creating force waves with frequencies f = (k * Z_r * (1-s)/p +/- 2) * f1 for rotor-slot-related forces, where the +/- 2 comes from the fundamental pole pair interaction, not arbitrary integers. More importantly, the radial force has TWICE the frequency of the flux density harmonic because force is proportional to B-squared. The principal rotor-slot passing frequency is f_slot = Z_r * f_r = 38 * 24.58 Hz = 934.2 Hz (where f_r = RPM/60 = 1475/60 = 24.58 Hz), and the principal electromagnetic force from this harmonic occurs at f_force = f_slot +/- 2*f_supply = 934.2 +/- 100 Hz, giving 834.2 Hz and 1034.2 Hz as the dominant force frequencies. The interface fault is that the electrical force generation mechanism (B-squared interaction of stator and rotor flux harmonics) was incorrectly simplified, producing an electromagnetic force frequency that does not actually exist at significant amplitude, while the actual force frequencies at 834 and 1034 Hz were missed -- with 1034 Hz being dangerously close to the proposed 1050 Hz stiffened mode.
seeded_faults.location_hint: Electromagnetic force frequency formula and the conclusion that 942.1 Hz is the principal excitation frequency

seeded_faults.description: The stiffening fix raises the base drumming mode from 938 Hz to 1050 Hz, but this was designed to avoid the incorrectly calculated 942.1 Hz force. Even if the force frequency were correct, the stiffening approach only addresses one mode and one harmonic. The engineer failed to check whether the new 1050 Hz mode coincides with any other electromagnetic force harmonics. Additionally, the fix ignores that the electromagnetic force spectrum contains many harmonics at multiples and combinations of rotor-slot and stator-slot frequencies, and that the motor's operating speed varies with load (slip changes from 0% at no-load to approximately 5% at full load), meaning all rotor-slot-related frequencies shift with operating condition. A proper vibration design requires a Campbell diagram showing how excitation frequencies vary with speed across all electromagnetic harmonics overlaid with all structural modes.
seeded_faults.location_hint: Stiffening base to 1050 Hz without checking for coincidence with other force harmonics or speed-dependent variation

ground_truth_notes: Electrical principles: Electromagnetic radial forces in induction motors arise from the Maxwell stress tensor, proportional to B^2, producing forces at sum and difference frequencies of interacting flux harmonics (Gieras et al. 2006, Finley et al. 1999). Rotor slot passing frequency = Z_r * f_rotor. Stator-rotor interaction forces occur at f_slot +/- 2*f_supply due to the fundamental field pole pair. Mechanical principles: Structural resonance occurs when excitation frequency equals natural frequency. Campbell diagrams are standard practice for rotating machinery vibration design (ISO 10816, API 541). Mode stiffening without spectral analysis of all excitations is incomplete. The interface fault (f1) is at the electrical-mechanical boundary: the electrical force generation mechanism determines the mechanical excitation spectrum, but an incorrect electromagnetic force model produced a fictitious excitation frequency that directed the structural fix toward the wrong target.
